HEADLINE: Netanyahu claims Iran may try to disrupt election, warns, 'Don't test us'

THE SETTING — THIS IS WHAT MAKES IT AN ITEM
- BENJAMIN NETANYAHU, Prime Minister of Israel, speaking while STANDING AT AN ARROW ANTI-BALLISTIC MISSILE BATTERY, two days before Israel's general election on Tuesday.

VERBATIM QUOTES, ALL NETANYAHU
- "The IDF is prepared in both defense and offense."
- "We have intelligence signs that Iran and its proxies could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections."
- "I warn them. Don't test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows."
- "We are much stronger than you think. Don't underestimate us. Don't test us."

THE INTELLIGENCE CLAIM — LABEL IT AS HIS CLAIM
- Netanyahu said he possessed intelligence indications that Iran and allied forces might launch attacks timed to disrupt the election. NO EVIDENCE IS PUBLISHED. This is the Israeli prime minister's assertion, made at a missile battery, two days before he faces voters. Write it as his claim, not as a fact.

THE CONTRADICTION — THE SHARPEST LINE AVAILABLE AND IT IS SOURCED
- The Times of Israel notes a Channel 13 report that the IDF Chief of Staff, LT. GEN. EYAL ZAMIR, recently said he saw NO OPERATIONAL NECESSITY for striking Iran before the election — cutting against Netanyahu's posture of imminent threat.
- CHANNEL 13 IS NOT IN SOURCES.md. The Times of Israel is the approved source reporting it. If you use it, write "the Times of Israel reports that Israel's military chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, saw no operational need to strike Iran before the vote". Do not cite Channel 13.
- The piece also notes Netanyahu has contradicted his own statements of past months that Iran's nuclear programme had been "devastated" and that Tehran could no longer threaten Israel's existence, instead sharing a post referring to a "tangible existential threat".

SECOND APPROVED SOURCE: YES, CBS NEWS. Its Iran live file (last updated 13:22 EDT = 17:22 GMT) carries Netanyahu in a "video statement, Sunday": "Don't test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows." CBS describes it as a video statement; the Times of Israel places him at an Arrow battery. Those are compatible but not identical — if you name the setting, attribute it to the Times of Israel.

HOW THIS FITS TONIGHT'S IRAN PICTURE — THE TWO LEADERS ARE PULLING OPPOSITE WAYS ON THE SAME DAY
- Trump, later: "There will not be a strike today." (EVE-GEO-TimesOfIsrael-trump-no-strike-today.txt)
- Netanyahu, earlier the same afternoon, at a missile battery: "Don't test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows."
- Israel's own military chief, per the Times of Israel: no operational need to strike before Tuesday.
That three-way split is a cleaner, better-sourced story than either quote alone.
